title: The Crown of the Glass Steppe
premise: August Okafor has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where the god Veyl went silent and magic cannot follow, working as a mercenary for people who value her discretion. When a dying courier presses a map into her hands, she learns the silence was engineered: the god's voice was stolen and bound into the crown of King Aldric, where something ancient now wears him like a glove. August must cross the Glass Steppe, gathering allies who remember what was taken, to unbind king and god before the long winter seals the world. She succeeds only by giving up her own memories of the valley—and of the man she loves—paying survival's price so that love, duty, and memory can finally be set free.
about_author: Zephyrine Almeida is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped river deltas on three continents before turning to maps of imaginary places instead. She writes in a converted lighthouse, fueled by black tea and an abiding suspicion that every border is a story someone agreed to stop telling.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: August Okafor's POV. A routine protection job in the Hollow goes wrong when bandits mention a name from August's childhood—a name no one should remember. The valley's enforced amnesia feels thinner than usual. Emotional beat: unease beneath competence; the first crack in the life she built.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: August's POV. A dying courier collapses at the river ford, pressing a wax-sealed map into August's hands and whispering 'the crown remembers.' His wounds are wrong—not made by any blade she knows. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility; the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: August's POV, intercut with letters from her late mentor. The map shows the Glass Steppe but its center is blank, and ink moves when unwatched. Her mentor's letters hint she knew about the silent god. Emotional beat: grief braided with curiosity; choosing to investigate rather than burn the map.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Question
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes POV, August's oldest friend and fellow mercenary. Tomas notices August lying for the first time in fifteen years of partnership and follows her to the valley's edge. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by secrets; love he has never named.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: August's POV. Crossing the boundary line, August feels magic return like pressure in her ears—and hears, faintly, a god's heartbeat under the ground. Behind her, the valley forgets she existed. Emotional beat: vertigo and liberation; there is no going back.

chapters.title: Salt and Glass
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Steppe itself: crystallized remains of an old battlefield where memory pools like water. August drinks from a glass pool and relives a memory that isn't hers—a king begging forgiveness. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Sefa, a steppe-dweller who trades in bottled memories. She recognizes the map's hand as her missing father's and demands passage in exchange for guiding August. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two women using each other honestly.

chapters.title: Winter's Advance Guard
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The long winter arrives early—snow that erases footprints, names, and eventually faces. They shelter with refugees who have forgotten why they fled. Emotional beat: the stakes become flesh; forgetting as horror, not mercy.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following the heartbeat, they find Veyl's body—a mountain range shaped like a sleeping figure, its mouth sewn shut with silver thread. Something has been feeding on it for centuries. Emotional beat: righteous fury; the crime becomes personal.

chapters.title: Crownsguard
chapters.summary: New POV: Captain Ilsa Vane, sent by the capital to retrieve the map. Ilsa serves the crown loyally but has begun dreaming the king's dreams without his permission. Emotional beat: duty at war with conscience; the antagonist who might be an ally.

chapters.title: The City of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: August's POV. The trio reaches Meridian, capital city, where citizens rent new identities to escape the winter's forgetting. August poses as a noblewoman; Tomas arrives, furious, and forces a reckoning. Emotional beat: confrontation and confession; love spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: August's POV. Granted court access, August sees King Aldric up close: lucid for seconds at a time, mouthing 'help me' behind a smiling mask. The thing in the crown looks directly at her and knows her name. Emotional beat: terror and pity entwined.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa confronts August privately, revealing the crown has been eating the king's memories for years and offering her guard rotation codes—if August swears the king dies free or not at all. Emotional beat: trust extended across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Archive of Unmade Things
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In the palace archives, Sefa finds her father's research: the crown was forged to imprison Veyl's voice, and unbinding requires a willing vessel of living memory. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; someone must pay, and everyone does the math.

chapters.title: What August Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. August realizes she qualifies: the valley preserved her memories precisely because it erased everything else. She begins writing down her life—every memory she'll lose—to leave instructions for herself. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; love measured in pages.

chapters.title: The Night of Long Snow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The winter breaches the city walls; whole districts go blank mid-sentence. Ilsa buys them one hour by arresting her own soldiers. Tomas refuses to let August face the crown alone. Emotional beat: siege intimacy; courage as a shared act.

chapters.title: Throne of Thread and Silver
chapters.summary: August's POV. The infiltration. August reaches the throne room and speaks Veyl's true name—the first word of the song the god sang to make the world. The crown screams. Aldric's eyes clear for one full minute. Emotional beat: the climax ignites; a king remembered as a man.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: August's POV. To sever the binding, August offers herself as vessel—but Tomas takes her place halfway through the rite, pouring his memories of her into the crown to complete it. The thing wearing the crown unravels; Veyl's voice returns as dawn light. Emotional beat: sacrifice, grief, and the god's first word in centuries: 'enough.'

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Voice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. With the crown destroyed, Ilsa arrests the ministers who forged it, then kneels to a king who barely knows his own reign. Aldric chooses abdication over a throne built on theft. Emotional beat: accountability; institutions forced to face their founding sin.

chapters.title: The Price, Tallied
chapters.summary: August's POV. August wakes with pages in her pocket written in her own hand and no memory of writing them. She reads her life like a stranger's story—her mother, her mercenary years, Tomas. Emotional beat: mourning someone still alive; herself.

chapters.title: Spring on the Steppe
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The winter breaks. Sefa buries her father's map at the site of Veyl's sleeping form, now humming audibly. August, reading her own journals daily, chooses to stay near Tomas and learn herself again rather than return to a valley that forgot her. Emotional beat: tender reconstruction; love as relearning.

chapters.title: The Crown of the Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: August's POV, coda. On the anniversary, August stands where the god's heartbeat is loudest. Veyl, restored but diminished, offers to return what she lost. August declines some memories and accepts others—including, finally, the feeling of being loved. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given; the price paid becomes a life chosen.
